pr.title: Send client credentials as UTF-8
pr.body:
## Summary

When the server logs on to another server as a client, it now sends its credentials as **UTF-8**. Until now they went in the Windows system code page, so a password containing `ä`, `✓` or a CJK character didn't work on the other server. The #21 route tests found this.

## Where it applied

| Client | Credentials | Before |
|---|---|---|
| SMTP, to the server a route relays through | AUTH LOGIN user name and password | `StringParser::Base64Encode` converted the text to the code page before base64-encoding it |
| POP3, to an external account's server | `USER` and `PASS` | `EnqueueWrite` converted the text to the code page |

So `ä` arrived as one byte that isn't valid UTF-8, and a character outside the code page (`✓`, CJK) was dropped entirely.

## Changes

- **`Unicode::ToUTF8`**: a string's exact UTF-8 bytes, without the stray terminating null that `WideToMultiByte` leaves in its output (seen in #17).
- **`SMTPClientConnection`** base64-encodes the UTF-8 of the AUTH LOGIN user name and password.
- **`POP3ClientConnection`** sends `USER` and `PASS` through a new `EnqueueWriteUtf8_`. The log still masks the password as `***`.

`StringParser::Base64Encode` is unchanged, because its other callers, such as the SMTP server's own `Username:`/`Password:` prompts, only encode ASCII.

## Tests

`Security.ClientCredentialsEncoding` uses a user name and password containing `ü`/`ä`, `✓` and `漢`:

- **`TestRouteAuthenticatesInUtf8`**: the simulated SMTP server receives exactly that user name and password. `SmtpServerSimulator` now also records the AUTH LOGIN user name.
- **`TestExternalAccountLogsOnInUtf8`**: `Pop3ServerSimulator` now records `USER` and `PASS`.
  - The simulator reads plain connections as ASCII, so each byte above 127 shows up as `?`.
  - The test therefore expects one `?` per UTF-8 byte: two for `ü`, three for `✓`.
  - The old code-page encoding would give one `?` or none, so the test tells the two apart.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commit.message:
Send client credentials as UTF-8

The credentials the server sends as a client went in the system code page:
AUTH LOGIN to the server a route relays through (StringParser::Base64Encode
converts to it before encoding), and USER and PASS to the POP3 server of an
external account (the String to AnsiString conversion of EnqueueWrite). A
password with an a-umlaut reached the other server as one byte that is not
UTF-8, and a character outside the code page - a check mark, any CJK
character - not at all, so the other server refused the logon. Found by the
route tests of #21.

- Unicode::ToUTF8 returns a string's UTF-8 bytes exactly, without the
  terminating null WideToMultiByte leaves in what it returns.
- SMTPClientConnection base64-encodes the UTF-8 of the AUTH LOGIN user name and
  password.
- POP3ClientConnection sends USER and PASS through EnqueueWriteUtf8_; the log
  still shows the password as ***.

StringParser::Base64Encode itself is left as it is: the SMTP server's own
prompts and other callers use it for ASCII only.

Tests (Security.ClientCredentialsEncoding), with a user name and password that
have an a-umlaut, a check mark and a CJK character:
- a route authenticates with them as UTF-8; SmtpServerSimulator now records
  the AUTH LOGIN user name too;
- an external account logs on with them as UTF-8; Pop3ServerSimulator records
  USER and PASS. It reads a plain connection as ASCII, so the test expects one
  '?' for each UTF-8 byte above 127 - two for the u-umlaut, three for the check
  mark - where the code page left one, or none.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Wait for the fetched message before the UTF-8 POP3 test ends

The next test's setup deleted the account while the message was still being
delivered, which logged HM5165 and failed that test's teardown.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
